card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 That Suddenly Developed a No Service Issue. Baseband Repair

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 7 That Suddenly Developed a No Service Issue. Baseband Repair

claims.statement: A never-repaired iPhone 7 showing Searching/No Service without a SIM (instead of No SIM), no IMEI and blank modem firmware has a baseband fault.
Intel models: the BBPMU_RF (part 6826) has failed and is replaced.
Qualcomm models: check for shorts around BBPMU; if none, replace it and jumper corner ground pads 98, 93, 88, 83 to the ground layer. A short on PP_0V9_LDO3 points at XCVR0_RF / XCVR1_RF.

PP_1V0_SMPS5 reading about 0.100–0.125 in diode mode is a partial short that can be bypassed with a 1K resistor from C5701_RF and a jumper to C5627_RF (PP_1V2_LDO2); 0.000 means internal baseband CPU short, which is not fixable because it is paired.
Restoring a phone with a baseband fault erases the IMEI; fix the board then restore again. After repair, flash an update (not restore) if still searching.

procedure: Check No SIM vs Searching, *#06#, and modem firmware field.
Qualcomm: check shorts around BBPMU; replace it and ground the corner pads.
Check PP_0V9_LDO3 and PP_1V0_SMPS5 diode values; apply XCVR or resistor workaround as applicable.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
